lf-reel-1024-grandma-resp.caption:
New dad, feeling left out? You don't need to feed the baby to bond with them.

Bonding is built in small, daily care: the same jobs, done by the same person, every day. Here's how to own a few.

1. OWN BATH TIME. Same time, same song, every night. Chat and play the whole way through. It becomes your thing.
2. SKIN TO SKIN. It works for partners too: shirt off, baby in just a diaper on your bare chest, a blanket over you both. Only when you're fully awake. Feeling sleepy? Baby goes on their back in their own crib.
3. TALK THROUGH THE DIAPER CHANGE. "Left leg… right leg! Where did your toes go? There they are!" Peekaboo counts.
4. ONE STORY, EVERY NIGHT. Babies enjoy hearing your voice long before they follow the words.

GIVE IT TIME: bonding doesn't always feel like a lightning bolt. Week 1 can feel like you're just the helper. By month 1, bath time is your routine together. Picture year 1: the one they reach for when the water's running.

Do this: tonight, take bath time. Same time, same song, your job, from now on.

The rule that stays: don't wait for a turn. Take a job.

Send this to a new dad, or any partner who feels like a spare pair of hands.

Follow for one calm thing a night, from bump to toddler.

General information only, not medical advice.

ff-reel-1024-beneficiary.caption:
Never named a TFSA beneficiary? Your TFSA has a blank line. Fill it in.

When you open a TFSA or RRSP, it asks who gets the money if you die. That person is your beneficiary (for a spouse on a TFSA, it can be a "successor holder").

Why it matters: with a name there, the money can go straight to that person, outside your estate. In Ontario, the estate administration tax is $15 for every $1,000 over $50,000, so $100,000 going through the estate costs about $750. Money paid to a named beneficiary isn't counted. It's also usually faster.

Do this tonight (10 minutes):
1. Log in to your bank or broker and open each TFSA, RRSP and FHSA.
2. Find "Beneficiary" or "Successor holder" (often under account details or documents). Blank, or an ex? Fix it.
3. Check your work life insurance and pension in your benefits portal too.
Moved in with someone, had a baby, or split up since you opened them? Update every one.

The rule to remember: life changed? Change the name.

Rules differ by province (in Quebec, most designations go in your will). Send this to your partner.

Follow for one money move a day, in plain words.

#beneficiary #TFSA #RRSP #estateplanning #moneyfoundations

Maths: ($100,000 − $50,000) ÷ 1,000 × $15 = $750. General information, not legal or tax advice.

ff-pan-1025am-paycheque-trail.caption:
Not married? No will? In Ontario, your partner may get nothing.

If you die without a will in Ontario, the law decides who inherits:
Married spouse: everything if the estate is under $350,000; otherwise the first $350,000, and the rest is shared with your children.
Common-law partner: nothing under these rules, even after years together. They may have to go to court to ask for support.

The fix is one will. It says who gets what, and who you'd want to raise your kids.

Do this: this week, book one call with a wills lawyer and ask, "What does a will and power of attorney cost for both of us?"

Other provinces have different rules, so check yours.

Send this to your partner.

Follow for one money move a day, in plain words.

#wills #estateplanning #commonlaw #personalfinancecanada #moneyfoundations

ff-reel-1025-tfsa-withdrawal-trap.caption:
Putting TFSA money back? Wait. Here's the trap.

You take out $5,000 in March and put it back in June. Feels harmless. But the room from a withdrawal only comes back on January 1 of the next year. If you had no other room left, that $5,000 is an over-contribution, and the CRA charges 1% a month on it until it's out: $50 a month, about $350 from June to December.

Do this: before you put money back, check your room in CRA My Account (it shows your room as of January 1). Moving money between banks? Ask for a direct transfer, which doesn't count as a withdrawal.

Already did it? Take the extra out as soon as you can, and look up form RC243 (the TFSA return) on canada.ca.

The rule to remember: out this year? Back in January.

Send this to your TFSA friend.

Follow for one money move a day, in plain words.

#TFSA #personalfinancecanada #CRA #taxtips #moneyfoundations
ff-reel-1025-tfsa-withdrawal-trap.first_comment: Sources: CRA (canada.ca), 'Before you contribute to a TFSA' and the TFSA withdrawal pages: withdrawals are added back to your contribution room at the beginning of the following year; an excess amount is taxed 1% per month for each month it stays in the account; direct transfers between your own TFSAs are not withdrawals; excess amounts are reported on form RC243. Your room as of January 1 is in CRA My Account (subtract this year's deposits). Maths: 1% of $5,000 = $50 for each month the excess stays in; June through December = 7 months = $350. Sunday night? Your whole week fits on one card. Five messages in, one line a day out.

Why it works: the week's deadlines hide in five different apps. Paste them in one place and the AI sorts them by day, so nothing waits in a chat you forgot to reopen.

Do this: paste the week's messages. Ask for one line a day.

The catch, from this exact run: the message said milk and dog food "before Tue". The AI put it on Tuesday. Check each line against the original message.

Made up for this post: all 5 messages. The reply is real (Claude, by Anthropic, run Oct 22, 2026), quoted exactly.

ff-1025-hold-cost-of-waiting.caption:
“I'll start next year.” Waiting from 25 to 27 costs about $212,200 at 60. Hold the dots and slide 👀

$300 a month until 60, growing 10% a year:
• Start at 25: about $1,139,000
• Start at 27: about $926,800
• Start at 29: about $752,900
• Start at 31: about $610,500
• Start at 33: about $493,700
• Start at 35: about $398,100

Waiting from 25 to 27 skips $7,200 of deposits, and costs about $212,200 at 60. Those first dollars have the most years to grow, so they're the most valuable dollars you'll ever invest.

Started later? You haven't lost; you just need a bigger monthly amount. The second-best time to start is today.

Do this: start this payday, even at $50 a month. You can raise it later.

Send this to your "I'll start next year" friend.

Not guaranteed. Returns vary. Education, not advice.

hb-1025-family-calendar.caption:
Too much AI news? Keep these 7 rules. One week, 7 rules for the AI age.

Day 1, agents: AI now clicks, scrolls and fills in forms for you. Rule: AI clicks. You press pay.
Day 2, hallucination: AI is trained in a way that rewards guessing over "I don't know". Rule: fluent isn't true.
Day 3, privacy: chats are stored, may train future models, and some are read by people. Rule: type it like a postcard, not a diary.
Day 4, your career: the skills inside jobs are changing fast. Rule: bring AI to everything, and stay the human in the loop.
Day 5, how it works: it predicts the next word-piece from patterns. Rule: a pattern machine, not a fact machine.
Day 6, the big idea: prediction got cheap, so judgment got valuable. Rule: AI predicts. You judge.
Day 7, it's already here: in WhatsApp, Gmail and your phone. Rule: learn it on purpose, not by accident.

lh-1025-climb-one-percent.caption:
Monday isn't magic. It's a handle. Grab it tonight.

THE RESEARCH: researchers looked at the gym records of about 12,000 students at one US university. At the start of a new week, the chance of a gym visit was 33.4% higher than usual. The start of a month: 14.4%. The start of a semester: 47.1%. They call it the fresh start effect: a new week feels like a clean page, so people try again.

THE HONEST PART: it's correlational. It shows when people start, not that Mondays make anything work. And it cuts both ways: waiting for Monday can turn into waiting forever.

HOW TO USE IT:
1. Tonight, pick one thing you want to start.
2. Write when and where: "Monday, 8 am, after coffee."
3. Missed it? Every day has a handle: tomorrow morning, after lunch, the next hour.

Do this: tonight, pick one thing and write when you'll start it: "Monday, 8 am, after coffee."

Send this to the friend waiting for a fresh start.

Follow for one small focus fix a day, each one backed by research.

#habits #freshstart #mondaymotivation #focus #selfimprovement
lh-1025-climb-one-percent.first_comment: When will you start yours? Source: Dai, Milkman & Riis (2014), The Fresh Start Effect: Temporal Landmarks Motivate Aspirational Behavior, Management Science 60(10). Study 2: gym attendance records of 11,912 undergraduates at a large northeastern US university, Sept 2010 to Dec 2011. The probability of a gym visit rose at the start of a week (33.4%), month (14.4%) and semester (47.1%), relative to baseline. Archival, correlational data.

hb-1025-hold-task-length.caption:
AI working alone: from 2-second tasks in 2019 to about an hour in early 2025. Hold the dots and slide 👀

METR, an AI research nonprofit, timed skilled people on software and research tasks, then measured which tasks AI agents could complete. Their key number is the "time horizon": the length of task (in human time) an AI finishes with 50% success.

In 2019, GPT-2: about 2 seconds. In early 2025, Claude 3.7 Sonnet: about an hour. Over those six years, it doubled roughly every 7 months. The jar shows that trend line, two doublings per swipe.

Why it matters: doubling looks like nothing for years, then fills the jar fast. METR's own caveats: these are mostly software tasks, 50% success isn't reliable, and trends can change. Newer models have been measured since; check metr.org for the latest.

Do this: next AI launch, skip the hype and ask one question: how long a task can it do on its own?

Send this to the friend who thinks AI peaked.

#ai #aiagents #futureofwork #metr #hourback
hb-1025-hold-task-length.first_comment: Surprised?
